question: Prove that the relation $R$ in the set $\mathbb{Z}$ of integers defined by $R = \{(a, b): a-b\text{ is divisible by }5\}$ is an equivalence relation, and find the set of all elements related to $7$.
explanation:
To prove $R$ is an equivalence relation:

Reflexivity: For any $a$, $a-a=0$ is divisible by $5$, so $(a,a)\in R$.

Symmetry: If $(a,b)\in R$ then $a-b$ is divisible by $5$, so $b-a=-(a-b)$ also divisible by $5$, so $(b,a)\in R$.

Transitivity: If $(a,b)\in R$ and $(b,c)\in R$, then $a-b$ and $b-c$ are divisible by $5$, so $(a-b)+(b-c)=a-c$ is divisible by $5$. So $(a,c)\in R$.

Consequently, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

Set of all elements related to $7$ are those $b$ such that $7-b$ divisible by $5$, i.e., $7-b=5k$ for some $k\in\mathbb{Z}$.

$\implies b=7-5k$ for all $k\in\mathbb{Z}$.

Or equivalently, $b\equiv 7\pmod{5} \implies b\equiv 2\pmod{5}$.

All integers congruent to $2 \pmod{5}$ are related to $7$.

options.A: $R$ is not an equivalence relation and no integer is related to $7$
options.B: $R$ is an equivalence relation and the elements related to $7$ are only $\{7\}$
options.C: $R$ is an equivalence relation and the elements related to $7$ are all multiples of $5$
options.D: $R$ is an equivalence relation and the elements related to $7$ are all integers congruent to $2\pmod{5}$
